Selling houses would return only half their value. Player 1 already has four houses on both dark blue properties, so they cannot build hotels even if houses were freed. The $163 from Ventnor mortgage is still insufficient for a hotel.

Standard Monopoly rent for four houses on Park Place is $1,300 and on Boardwalk is $1,700. Hotel upgrades would raise those to $1,500 and $2,000.

Liquidating the entire pink monopoly would yield roughly $980: $160 cash plus $600 from selling twelve houses at half price and $220 from mortgaging the three properties.

Even liquidating the entire pink monopoly would not make those dark blue properties survivable. Player 1's four-house rent on Park Place is $1,300 and on Boardwalk is $1,700. Hotel upgrades on the pink set would add only $150 to $200 per property. Player 4's light blue hotels cost just $50 each.

Player 4 could immediately upgrade all three light blue properties to hotels for $150 total. That would raise their rent by only $100 per property, which is a minor threat compared to the dark blue danger. Player 1 still cannot afford any hotel upgrades.

Player 4 owns North Carolina and a mortgaged Pennsylvania Avenue. They need Tennessee to complete their orange set, which is a major threat.

Unmortgaging the Pennsylvania Railroad would cost $110. That is too expensive with only $160 in cash.

Unmortgaging the Pennsylvania Railroad would only yield $25 in rent, so the $110 cost is not worthwhile. Unmortgaging Tennessee would also be a waste of cash, since player 4 already owns two other orange properties and would not gain a monopoly without them.

Trading Tennessee to player 4 would complete their orange set, which is extremely dangerous. Player 4 currently has no houses in the bank, so they cannot build hotels immediately, but giving them that property is still a major long-term threat.

Player 4 could pay up to $800, but that still leaves me with only about $1,780 in total liquid assets. That barely covers Boardwalk at four houses. Destroying my entire pink monopoly to survive one hit would be a terrible trade. I would rather try to acquire player 1's dark blue properties.

Player 1 cannot trade their dark blue properties while they have four houses on each. I will keep my Get Out of Jail Free card to sit in jail before landing on the dark blues. The plan is to end this turn without building, selling, unmortgaging, or trading.

The win condition is simply outlasting the other two players, since player 3 is already bankrupt. Player 1 could also land on my pink properties and force me to sell dark blue houses, which would weaken my own kill shot.

From there, a roll of 2 lands on Oriental Avenue ($450), 3 on Chance, 4 on Vermont ($450), 5 on Connecticut ($500), and 6 on Just Visiting. Player 4 can pay any of those dark blue rents without selling assets.

Rolling 2, 4, or 5 on the pink properties would require selling five houses each, which is still survivable.

If I go bankrupt to player 1, he would gain my pink monopoly and the houses would return to the bank so he could rebuild both sets. That would strengthen him against player 4. Bankruptcy to player 4 would also leave me dead.
